paper_metadata.title: Application of quantum computing in healthcare billing - USA

experiments.description: Theoretical QAOA-style optimization of healthcare billing code assignment to minimize cost and fraud/error risk under one-code-per-claim constraints.

algorithm.variant: QAOA for QUBO-like healthcare billing optimization

hyperparameters.lambda: weighting parameter balancing direct cost and error/fraud risk

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary decision variables x_ij indicate whether billing code j is assigned to claim i; the paper states this is encoded into qubit states for QAOA.
problem_formulation.objective_function: min sum_{i,j}(C_ij * x_ij) + lambda * sum_{i,j}(E_ij * x_ij) subject to sum_j x_ij = 1 for all i and x_ij in {0,1}.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Equality constraint sum_j x_ij = 1 for each claim; no explicit penalty formulation is given, but the text describes a QUBO-like mapping to a Hamiltonian.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H = sum_{i,j} C_ij sigma_z_i sigma_z_j + lambda * sum_{i,j} E_ij sigma_z_i sigma_z_j

problem_instance.description: Generic healthcare billing code-to-claim assignment optimization problem; no concrete dataset or instance size is provided.

dataset_specification.description: Anonymized healthcare billing datasets are mentioned in general terms, but no specific dataset, split, or preprocessing pipeline is reported.

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: The paper provides theoretical derivations and benchmark estimates rather than a reported empirical protocol.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Anonymized healthcare billing data collection is described at a high level.
implementation_details.quantum_execution_time: Estimated as ~10,000 gates on a processor carrying out ~1,000 gates/sec; the paper does not give a separate measured runtime for this optimization task.

results.unit: seconds (approximate estimate from 10,000 gates at 1,000 gates/sec)

speedup_claims.factor: NP-hard classical optimization vs QAOA mapping to QUBO/Hamiltonian
speedup_claims.conditions: for healthcare billing code assignment optimization
speedup_claims.caveats: No empirical benchmark is reported; the paper only states the problem is NP-hard and that QAOA can represent it as a Hamiltonian.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Not explicitly stated beyond QAOA mapping to a Hamiltonian and general NP-hard/QUBO-like characterization.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: NP-hard (as stated for the binary optimization problem); no tighter bound is given.

experiments.description: Theoretical Grover-search-based fraud detection over healthcare claims to identify anomalous or fraudulent billing records.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Claims are searched via an oracle f(x) that marks whether a claim is fraudulent; the paper does not specify a detailed qubit encoding beyond oracle-based search.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Search for fraudulent claims among N healthcare claims, where a fraction M << N are suspicious.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Oracle marking of fraudulent claims; no additional constraint handling is described.

problem_instance.description: Generic fraud detection over large healthcare billing databases; no concrete dataset or instance size is provided.

dataset_specification.description: No named dataset, date range, or split is reported.

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: The paper gives asymptotic complexity and a runtime estimate based on gate count, not a measured experimental protocol.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Anonymized healthcare billing data collection is described at a high level.
implementation_details.quantum_execution_time: Estimated runtime is ~50 seconds using 50,000 gates at ~1,000 gates/sec with efficiency factor 0.9; this is a paper estimate, not a measured runtime.

speedup_claims.conditions: for unstructured search over N healthcare claims with M << N suspicious claims
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper gives asymptotic complexity only; no empirical benchmark is reported.

speedup_claims.conditions: fraud/anomaly search in large healthcare billing databases
speedup_claims.caveats: Claim is based on Grover's algorithm; no measured speedup on real data is shown.

complexity_analysis.wall_clock_quantum: Approximately 50 seconds for a 50,000-gate job, per the paper's estimate.
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_classical: Minutes to hours, depending on algorithmic complexity and data volume, per the paper's estimate.
